title: Developing Communication Skills and Rifq with the Child in the First Months of Life
reference_info: CDC — Learn the Signs. Act Early: قوائم مراحل النمو (Milestone Checklists)
text_original: your baby. Act excited, smile, and talk to him when he makes sounds. This teaches him to take turns “talking” back and forth in conversation. • Talk, read, and sing to your baby to help her develop and understand language. • Spend time cuddling and holding your baby. This will help him feel safe and cared for. You will not spoil your baby by holding or responding to him. • Being responsive to your baby helps him learn and grow. Limiting your screen time when you are with your baby helps you be responsive. • Take care of yourself. Parenting can be hard work! It’s easier to enjoy your new baby when you feel good • Learn to notice and respond to your baby’s signals to know what she’s feeling and needs. You will feel good and your baby will feel safe and loved. For example, is she trying to “play” with you by making sounds and looking at you, or is she turning her head away, yawning, or becoming fussy because she • Lay your baby on his tummy when he is awake and put toys at eye level in front of him. This will help him practice lifting his head up. Do not leave your baby alone. If he seems sleepy, place him on his back in a safe sleep area (firm mattress with no blankets, pillows, bumper pads, or toys). • Feed only breast milk or formula to your baby. text_simplified: Talk to your child and make them feel at ease—this helps them learn communication. Read books and sing songs to your child to aid in developing their language skills.

review_defects.why: The Arabic word 'الرفق' means 'gentleness' or 'kindness', but the English transliterates it as 'Rifq' without translation, so the meaning is not conveyed to an English reader.

review_defects.english: Read books and sing songs to your child
review_defects.why: The Arabic says 'read books and songs' (قراءة كتب وأغاني), but the English changes the verb for songs to 'sing', adding an action not present in the Arabic.
